summary: Announces a questionnaire sent to every host on the early ARPANET. The answers about each machine's terminals and operation were meant to help the people designing a full Telnet specification. A small committee would phone each site to record answers and publish the results as an RFC; RFC 112 later summarized them.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC is a survey form about host computers and their terminals. The answers were meant to help people plan a fuller TELNET protocol.

subtitle: A ten-question survey for learning how ARPANET hosts handled terminals and character input.

tldr.problem: People considering a full TELNET protocol needed information about how Network hosts and their terminals worked.
tldr.mechanism: A committee asks each host's Technical Liaison to complete a questionnaire, then plans to call the sites and record the answers.
tldr.outcome: The RFC contains the blank questionnaire and says the answers will be tabulated and distributed separately.

sections.title: Why the Committee Asked
sections.content:
RFC 106 says that information about Network host characteristics and operation would help implementers of early TELNET versions and the User/Server Site Protocol Committee. The Technical Liaison at each host is asked to review the form.

A committee member planned to contact each site by telephone to record its answers. The RFC says the results would later be tabulated and distributed as an RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: The committee wants to learn how each host works before settling on a full TELNET protocol. It plans to collect answers from the people responsible for each site.

sections.title: Terminal Input and Characters
sections.content:
The form asks whether a system handles keyboard input one character at a time, a line at a time, or both. It asks for maximum input and output line buffers and the effects of carriage return, line feed, newline, and their combinations.

It also asks which characters awaken a process during input, which terminal types and codes the system supports, and which internal character set it uses.
sections.plainLanguage: Several questions ask what happens when a person types, including whether the computer reacts to each character or waits for a whole line. The form also asks which keyboards and character codes the host understands.

sections.title: Other Questions and the Results
sections.content:
The remaining questions cover supported duplex modes, whether an optional-echo terminal is assumed to need echo at connection time, and whether terminal input receives error checks such as parity checking. The form also asks about punched paper tape and its end-of-line sequence.

RFC 106 prints questions only; it contains no completed host responses.
sections.plainLanguage: The form asks about echo, input errors, and paper-tape terminals. This RFC is blank, so it does not report any host's answers.
